units.zh: 毛璋，本滄州小校。
units.en: Mao Zhang had begun his career as a low-ranking officer in Cangzhou.
units.literal: Mao Zhang was originally a petty officer of Cangzhou.

units.zh: 梁將戴思遠帥滄州，時莊宗已定魏博，思遠勢蹙，棄州遁去，璋據城歸莊宗，
units.en: When Liang general Dai Siyuan held Cangzhou, Emperor Zhuangzong had already secured Weibo. With his position collapsing, Siyuan abandoned the prefecture and fled, and Zhang seized the city and submitted to Zhuangzong,
units.literal: Liang general Dai Siyuan commanded Cangzhou. At that time Emperor Zhuangzong had already pacified Weibo; Siyuan's position was desperate, and he abandoned the prefecture and fled. Zhang held the city and submitted to Zhuangzong,

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：戴思遠任浮陽日，有部曲毛璋，為性輕悍。
units.en: (According to Tales from the Jade Hall: While Dai Siyuan was governing Fuyang, one of his retainers was Mao Zhang, known for his reckless, aggressive nature.
units.literal: (Tales from the Jade Hall: When Dai Siyuan was stationed at Fuyang, among his troops was Mao Zhang, a man of rash and fierce temperament.

units.zh: 嘗與數十卒追捕盜賊，還宿於逆旅，毛枕劍而寢。
units.en: On one occasion he took several dozen men in pursuit of bandits. On the way back they put up at an inn, and Mao went to sleep with his sword under his head.
units.literal: Once, with several dozen soldiers, he pursued bandits and on the return lodged at an inn; Mao slept with his sword as a pillow.

units.zh: 夜分，其劍忽大吼，躍出鞘外，從卒聞者愕然驚異，毛亦神之。
units.en: At midnight his sword suddenly gave a great roar and jumped clear of its scabbard. The soldiers who heard it were stunned; Mao, too, regarded the event as an omen.
units.literal: In the middle of the night, his sword suddenly roared and leapt from its scabbard. The accompanying soldiers who heard it were startled and amazed; Mao also took it as a supernatural sign.

units.zh: 乃持劍祝曰：「某若異日有此山河，爾當更鳴躍，否則已。」
units.en: Taking the sword in hand, he addressed it: "If I should one day come to rule these lands, you will roar and leap again; if not, let this be the end of it."
units.literal: He then took up the sword and prayed: "If I one day come to possess this realm of mountains and rivers, you shall roar and leap again; if not, let it be so no more."

units.zh: 毛復寢，未熟，劍吼躍如初，毛深自負。
units.en: Mao went back to sleep. Before he had settled into deep slumber, the sword roared and leapt again just as before. From that moment he was convinced of his destiny.
units.literal: Mao slept again, and before he had fallen deeply asleep, the sword roared and leapt as before. Mao greatly congratulated himself.

units.zh: 其後戴離鎮，毛請留，戴從之。
units.en: When Dai later left his command, Mao asked to stay behind, and Dai agreed.
units.literal: Later, when Dai left his post, Mao asked to remain behind, and Dai granted his request.

units.zh: 未幾，毛以州歸命於唐莊宗，莊宗以毛為其州刺史，後竟帥滄海。）〉
units.en: Not long afterward Mao turned the prefecture over to Tang Emperor Zhuangzong, who made him prefect of that prefecture; he eventually rose to command the Canghai circuit.)〉
units.literal: Before long, Mao surrendered the prefecture to Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, who appointed Mao prefect of that prefecture; in the end he came to command the Canghai circuit.)〉

units.zh: 曆貝州、遼州刺史。
units.en: He later served in turn as prefect of Beizhou and Liaozhou.
units.literal: He successively served as prefect of Beizhou and Liaozhou.

units.zh: 璋性凶悖，有膽略，從征河上，屢有戰功。
units.en: Zhang was violent and lawless by nature, yet bold and capable. On campaigns along the Yellow River he won repeated martial honors.
units.literal: Zhang was by nature violent and defiant, but bold and resourceful. Campaigning on the Yellow River front, he repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.

units.zh: 梁平，授滄州節度使。
units.en: After the Liang dynasty fell, he was made military commissioner of Cangzhou.
units.literal: When the Liang was pacified, he was appointed military commissioner of Cangzhou.

units.zh: 王師討蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬軍都指揮使；
units.en: During the imperial campaign against Shu, he was appointed overall commander of the right-wing cavalry in the field headquarters;
units.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, Zhang was made commander-in-chief of the right-wing cavalry of the field headquarters;

units.zh: 蜀平，璋功居多。
units.en: After Shu was pacified, Zhang's contribution ranked among the greatest.
units.literal: When Shu was pacified, Zhang's achievements ranked foremost among all.

units.zh: 明年，蕭牆禍起，繼岌自西川至渭南，部下散亡，其川貨妓樂，為璋所掠。
units.en: The following year, palace intrigue erupted into disaster. As Li Jiji made his way from western Sichuan to Weinan, his forces melted away, and Zhang seized the Sichuan wealth, entertainers, and musicians in his train.
units.literal: The next year, calamity arose within the palace walls. Jiji came from western Sichuan to Weinan; his followers scattered and fled, and the Sichuan goods, courtesans, and musicians were plundered by Zhang.

units.zh: 明宗嗣位，錄平蜀功，授邠州節度使。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Zhang's role in the conquest of Shu was formally acknowledged, and he was given Binzhou as his circuit.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, Zhang's service in pacifying Shu was recognized, and he was appointed military commissioner of Binzhou.

units.zh: 璋既家富於財，有蜀之妓樂，驕僭自大，動多不法，招致部下，繕理兵仗。
units.en: Flush with wealth and in possession of Shu's courtesans and musicians, Zhang grew arrogant and overbearing. He habitually flouted the law, gathering followers and stockpiling arms.
units.literal: Zhang was now wealthy and possessed the entertainers and musicians of Shu. He became arrogant and overbearing, frequently acting unlawfully, recruiting followers, and outfitting weapons and armor.

units.zh: 朝廷移授昭義節度使，璋謀欲不奉詔，判官邊蔚密言規責，乃僶勉承命。
units.en: When the court reassigned him to the Zhaoyi circuit, Zhang considered defying the order. Only after his secretary Bian Wei quietly reprimanded him did he grudgingly accept.
units.literal: The court transferred him to the Zhaoyi military commissionership. Zhang planned to refuse the decree, but his aide Bian Wei privately admonished him, and he reluctantly accepted.

units.zh: 洎至潞州，狂妄不悛，每擁川妓於山亭院，服赭黃，縱酒，令為王衍在蜀之戲。
units.en: Once at Luzhou he remained as reckless as ever. He often gathered Sichuan courtesans in the Mountain Pavilion courtyard, dressed in imperial ochre-yellow, drank heavily, and had them reenact the amusements of Wang Yan's court in Shu.
units.literal: When he reached Luzhou, he remained brazen and unrepentant. He regularly surrounded himself with Sichuan courtesans in the Mountain Pavilion courtyard, wore ochre-yellow robes, indulged in wine, and had them perform the entertainments Wang Yan had enjoyed in Shu.

units.zh: 事聞於朝，征為金吾上將軍。
units.en: When the court learned of this, he was recalled to serve as Senior General of the Golden Guard.
units.literal: When word reached the court, he was summoned to serve as Senior General of the Golden Guard.

units.zh: 其年秋，東川節度使董璋上言：「毛璋男廷贇齎父書往西川，慮有陰事。」
units.en: That autumn, Dong Zhang, military commissioner of Dongchuan, memorialized: "Mao Zhang's son Tingyun is carrying a letter from his father to western Sichuan, and I fear some covert design lies behind the journey."
units.literal: That autumn, Dongchuan military commissioner Dong Zhang memorialized: "Mao Zhang's son Tingyun, bearing a letter from his father, is going to western Sichuan; I fear there is a secret plot."

units.zh: 因追廷贇及同行人趙延祚，與璋俱下御史台獄。
units.en: On that basis Tingyun and his traveling companion Zhao Yanzuo were seized, and Mao Zhang was imprisoned by the censorate as well.
units.literal: On this account Tingyun and his companion Zhao Yanzuo were apprehended, and Mao Zhang was also sent to the censorate prison.

units.zh: 廷贇乃璋之假侄，稱有叔在蜀，欲往省之，亦無私書，詔停任，令歸私第。
units.en: Tingyun was Zhang's adoptive nephew. He said he had an uncle in Shu whom he wished to visit, and no secret letter was found. An edict relieved Zhang of his post and ordered him home.
units.literal: Tingyun was Zhang's adoptive nephew. He claimed to have an uncle in Shu and wished to visit him, and there was in fact no secret letter. An edict suspended Zhang's office and ordered him to return to his private residence.

units.zh: 初，延祚在獄，多言璋陰事，璋許重賂，以塞其口。
units.en: While Zhao Yanzuo was in custody, he testified at length about Zhang's covert activities. Zhang promised him a large bribe to keep quiet.
units.literal: At first, while in prison Zhao Yanzuo spoke at length of Zhang's secret dealings. Zhang promised him a heavy bribe to silence him.

units.zh: 及免，延祚征其賂，璋拒而不與，以至延祚詣台訴璋翻覆，復下御史台訊鞫。
units.en: After Yanzuo was freed, he demanded payment, but Zhang refused. Yanzuo then returned to the censorate and accused Zhang of going back on his word, and Zhang was again taken into custody for questioning.
units.literal: When he was released, Yanzuo demanded the bribe, but Zhang refused to pay. Yanzuo therefore went to the censorate and accused Zhang of duplicity, and Zhang was again imprisoned for interrogation.

units.zh: 中丞呂夢奇以璋前蒙昭雪，今延祚以責賂之故，復加織羅，故稍佑璋。
units.en: Censor-in-chief Lü Mengqi felt that Zhang had already been cleared once and that Yanzuo was now pressing the case only because a promised bribe had not been paid. Believing the new accusations were contrived, he leaned somewhat in Zhang's favor.
units.literal: Censor-in-chief Lü Mengqi, considering that Zhang had previously been cleared and that Yanzuo, now pursuing him over a failed bribe, was fabricating charges again, and thus he slightly favored Zhang.

units.zh: 及款狀上聞，或云夢奇受璋賂，所以獄不盡情，執之，移於軍巡。
units.en: When the written confession reached the throne, some said Lü Mengqi had taken a bribe from Zhang and had therefore not pursued the case fully. Mengqi was arrested himself, and the investigation was transferred to the military patrol office.
units.literal: When the confession was reported upward, some said Mengqi had accepted a bribe from Zhang, and therefore the investigation was not fully pursued. He was arrested and the case transferred to the military patrol office.

units.zh: 璋具狀曾許延祚賂未與，又云曾借馬與夢奇，別無行賂之事。
units.en: Zhang's full statement acknowledged that he had promised Yanzuo a bribe but never paid it, and that he had once lent a horse to Mengqi, but denied any other bribery.
units.literal: Zhang stated in full that he had promised Yanzuo a bribe but had not paid it, and also that he had once lent a horse to Mengqi, but that there was no other bribery.

units.zh: 朝廷懲其宿惡，長流儒州，賜死於路。
units.en: The court, punishing his long record of misconduct, banished him to Ruzhou and ordered him put to death on the way.
units.literal: The court punished his long-standing wickedness by banishing him to Ruzhou and ordering his death en route.

units.zh: 聶嶼，鄴中人。
units.en: Nie Yu came from Ye.
units.literal: Nie Yu was a native of Ye.

units.zh: 少為僧，漸學吟詠。
units.en: As a youth he entered the monastic life and gradually learned to write poetry.
units.literal: In youth he became a monk and gradually learned to compose verse.

units.zh: 鄭玨之再主禮闈也，與鄉人趙都俱赴鄉薦，都納賄於玨，人報翌日登第，嶼聞不捷，詬來人以嚇之，玨懼，俾俱成名。
units.en: When Zheng Jue again oversaw the civil examinations, Nie and his fellow townsman Zhao Du both sought provincial recommendation. Du paid Jue a bribe, and word spread that he would pass the next day. On learning he had failed, Nie cursed the messenger in a deliberate attempt to intimidate him. Frightened, Jue saw to it that both men passed.
units.literal: When Zheng Jue again presided over the civil examinations, Nie and his fellow townsman Zhao Du both submitted themselves for the provincial recommendation. Du paid a bribe to Jue, and someone reported that he would pass the next day. When Nie heard he had failed, he cursed the messenger to frighten him. Jue was afraid and had both men pass.

units.zh: 漸為拾遺，依郭崇韜為鎮州書記。
units.en: He eventually rose to the post of remonstrance officer and served under Guo Chongtao as secretary at Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: He gradually rose to Remonstrance Officer and attached himself to Guo Chongtao as secretary at Zhen Prefecture.

units.zh: 明宗時，為起居舍人。
units.en: Under Emperor Mingzong he served as a diarist.
units.literal: During the Mingzong reign he served as Diarist.

units.zh: 雙眸若懸，性氣乖僻，人多忌之。
units.en: His eyes bulged prominently, his temper was odd and difficult, and many came to dislike him.
units.literal: His two eyes bulged as if suspended; his temperament was perverse, and many people resented him.

units.zh: 天成初，除鄴都留守判官，與趙敬怡、呂夢奇不足。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era he was made aide to the Ye garrison commander and fell out with Zhao Jingyi and Lü Mengqi.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he was appointed aide to the Ye garrison commander, and he was on bad terms with Zhao Jingyi and Lü Mengqi.

units.zh: 又改河東節度，及至，常鄙其土風，薄其人士。
units.en: He was next posted to Hedong circuit, where he constantly sneered at the local ways and held its gentry in contempt.
units.literal: He was next transferred to Hedong circuit. When he arrived, he habitually looked down on its local customs and despised its people and scholars.

units.zh: 或達於重誨，會敬怡入為樞密使，與夢奇同構殺之。
units.en: Word of this reached An Chonghui. When Jingyi entered the capital as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he and Mengqi together plotted to have Nie killed.
units.literal: Some of this reached An Chonghui. When Jingyi entered the capital as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he joined with Mengqi in plotting Nie's death.

units.zh: 嶼早依郭崇韜門庭，致身朱紫，名登兩史，浙江使回，生涯巨萬。
units.en: Nie had risen through Guo Chongtao's patronage to high office, earned mention in both official histories, and after returning from an envoy mission to Zhejiang had accumulated a fortune numbering in the tens of thousands.
units.literal: Nie had early attached himself to Guo Chongtao's household, rose to wear purple and crimson, had his name recorded in both dynastic histories, and after returning from an envoy mission to Zhejiang amassed wealth in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 嶼內河東節判時，郭氏次子之婦，孀居於家，嶼喪偶未久，復忍而納幣，人皆罪之。
units.en: While serving as internal secretary and circuit judge in Hedong, Nie learned that the wife of Guo's second son was living at home as a widow. Though he had himself been widowed only recently, he brazenly sent betrothal gifts to her, to universal condemnation.
units.literal: While Nie was internal secretary and circuit judge in Hedong, the wife of Guo's second son was widowed at home. Nie had not long lost his own wife, yet he shamelessly sent betrothal gifts to her, and all condemned him.

units.zh: 明宗在藩邸時，素聞其醜聲。
units.en: Even when Mingzong was still a prince, he had heard repeated reports of Nie's disgraceful conduct.
units.literal: When Mingzong was still in his princely residence, he had long heard of Nie's ugly reputation.

units.zh: 天成中，與溫韜等同詔賜死。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era he was, by imperial edict together with Wen Tao and others, commanded to take his own life.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was, by edict along with Wen Tao and others, ordered to take his own life.

units.zh: 溫韜，華原人。
units.en: Wen Tao came from Huayuan.
units.literal: Wen Tao was a native of Huayuan.

units.zh: 少為盜，據華原，事李茂貞，名彥韜，後降於梁，更名昭圖。
units.en: As a youth he turned bandit, seized control of Huayuan, and entered Li Maozhen's service under the name Yan Tao. He later surrendered to the Liang and took the name Zhaotu.
units.literal: In youth he was a bandit who seized Huayuan and served Li Maozhen under the name Yan Tao. Later he surrendered to the Liang and changed his name to Zhaotu.

units.zh: 為耀州節度，唐諸陵在境者悉發之，取所藏金寶：而昭陵最固，悉藏前世圖書，鍾、王紙墨，筆跡如新。
units.en: As military commissioner of Yaozhou, he opened every Tang imperial tomb within his jurisdiction and looted the gold and treasures inside. The Zhao Mausoleum, the most securely built of all, held books and maps from earlier ages as well as calligraphy by Zhong You and Wang Xizhi—works whose ink looked as though it had been written yesterday.
units.literal: As military commissioner of Yaozhou, he opened every Tang imperial tomb within his jurisdiction and took the gold and treasures stored therein. The Zhao Mausoleum was the most secure and contained books and maps of former ages, paper and ink of Zhong and Wang, with brushwork as fresh as new.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
units.en: (Note: the text below is missing.)〉
units.literal: (Note: the text below is missing.)〉

units.zh: 移許州節度使，累官至檢校太尉、平章事。
units.en: He was transferred to Xuzhou as military commissioner and eventually rose to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor.
units.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Xuzhou and rose through successive posts to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 韜素善趙岩，每依附之。
units.en: Tao had long been close to Zhao Yan and habitually relied on his patronage.
units.literal: Tao had long been on good terms with Zhao Yan and constantly relied on him.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，岩恃韜與己素厚，遂奔許州。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yan counted on his long friendship with Tao and fled to Xuzhou.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yan relied on his old friendship with Tao and fled to Xuzhou.

units.zh: 韜延之於第，斬首傳送闕下。
units.en: Tao received him at his residence, beheaded him, and sent the head to the imperial court.
units.literal: Tao received him at his residence, beheaded him, and sent the head to the capital.

units.zh: 同光初，韜來朝，郭崇韜曰：「此劫陵賊，罪不可赦。」
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era, Tao came to court. Guo Chongtao said, "This tomb-raiding bandit—his crime cannot be forgiven."
units.literal: Early in the Tongguang era, Tao came to court. Guo Chongtao said: "This tomb-raiding bandit—his crime cannot be forgiven."

units.zh: 韜納賂劉後，賜姓，名紹衝，遽遣還鎮。
units.en: Tao bribed Empress Liu, was granted the imperial surname and the name Shaochong, and was promptly sent back to his post.
units.literal: Tao bribed Empress Liu, was granted the imperial surname and the name Shaochong, and was swiftly sent back to his command.

units.zh: 明宗即位，流於德州，俄賜死。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was exiled to Dezhou and soon commanded to take his own life.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was banished to Dezhou and soon ordered to take his own life.

units.zh: 長子延浚，清泰中為泥水關使；
units.en: His eldest son Yanjun served as commander of Nishui Pass during the Qingtai era;
units.literal: His eldest son Yanjun served as commander of Nishui Pass in the Qingtai era;

units.zh: 次延招，為父牙帳都校；
units.en: the second son Yanzhao was chief commandant of his father's personal guard;
units.literal: the second son Yanzhao was chief commandant of his father's personal guard;

units.zh: 次延袤，鄧州指揮使；
units.en: the third son Yanmao was commander at Deng Prefecture;
units.literal: the third son Yanmao was commander at Deng Prefecture;

units.zh: 鹹聚居許下。
units.en: They all lived together at Xuzhou.
units.literal: All lived together at Xuzhou.

units.zh: 晉天福初，聞張從賓作亂於河陽，鹹往依之。
units.en: Early in the Tianfu era of Jin, on hearing that Zhang Congbin had rebelled at Heyang, they all went to join him.
units.literal: Early in the Tianfu era of Jin, hearing that Zhang Congbin had rebelled at Heyang, they all went to join him.

units.zh: 從賓慮其難製，悉斬於帳下。
units.en: Congbin feared they would be difficult to control and had them all executed in his camp.
units.literal: Congbin feared they would be hard to control and had them all executed in his camp.

units.zh: 段凝，開封人也。
units.en: Duan Ning was a native of Kaifeng.
units.literal: Duan Ning was a native of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 本名明遠，少穎悟，多智數。
units.en: His original name was Mingyuan. As a youth he was quick-witted and adept at intrigue.
units.literal: His original name was Mingyuan. In youth he was quick-witted and full of stratagems.

units.zh: 初為澠池簿，脫荷衣以事梁祖，梁祖漸器之。
units.en: He began as a clerk in Mianchi County, then cast off his scholar's robe to enter the service of the Liang founder, who gradually came to esteem him.
units.literal: At first he was clerk of Mianchi County. He cast off his plain robe to serve the Liang founder, who gradually came to value him.

units.zh: 開平三年十月，自東頭供奉官授右威衛大將軍，充左軍巡使兼水北巡檢使。
units.en: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaiping he was promoted from Eastern Head Attendant to General of the Right Weiwu Guard, with concurrent duties as Left Army Patrol Commissioner and Northern Waters Inspector.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaiping, from Eastern Head Attendant he was appointed General of the Right Weiwu Guard, serving as Left Army Patrol Commissioner and concurrently Northern Waters Inspector.

units.zh: 凝妹為梁祖美人，故稍委心腹。
units.en: Ning's younger sister was a favored consort of the Liang founder, and on that account he was gradually treated as an inner-circle confidant.
units.literal: Ning's younger sister was a favored consort of the Liang founder, so he was gradually entrusted as a confidant.

units.zh: 四年五月，授懷州刺史。
units.en: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Huaizhou.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Huaizhou.

units.zh: 乾化元年十二月，梁祖北征回，過郡，凝貢獻加等，梁祖大悅。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qianhua, the Liang founder returned from a northern campaign and passed through his prefecture. Ning doubled his tribute, and the founder was greatly pleased.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qianhua, the Liang founder returned from a northern campaign and passed through the prefecture. Ning's tribute was doubled, and the founder was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 梁祖復北，凝迎奉進貢，有加於前。
units.en: When the founder marched north again, Ning received him with tribute even more lavish than before.
units.literal: When the founder marched north again, Ning welcomed him with tribute greater than before.

units.zh: 梁祖次相州，刺史李思安迎奉疏怠，梁祖怒，貶思安。
units.en: When the founder halted at Xiangzhou, Prefect Li Si'an received him with slack courtesy. The founder was enraged and demoted him.
units.literal: When the founder halted at Xiangzhou, Prefect Li Si'an received him negligently. The founder was angry and demoted Si'an.

units.zh: 製云：「懷州刺史段明遠，少年治郡，庶事惟公，兩度隻奉行鑾，數程宿食本界，動無遺闕，舉必周豐，蓋能罄竭於家財，務在顯酬夫明獎。
units.en: The edict declared: "Duan Mingyuan, prefect of Huaizhou, though young in governing a commandery, conducts every affair with scrupulous fairness. Twice he alone attended the imperial carriage; for several marches he provided lodging and provisions within his jurisdiction without a single lapse, and never with less than full abundance. He has clearly drained his family fortune and seeks thereby to make plain the value of enlightened reward.
units.literal: The edict read: "Duan Mingyuan, prefect of Huaizhou, though young in governing a commandery, handles every affair with fairness. Twice he alone attended upon the imperial carriage; for several marches he lodged and supplied provisions within his jurisdiction without omission in action or shortfall in provision. He has clearly exhausted his family wealth and strives to make manifest the reward of enlightened encouragement.

units.zh: 觀明遠之忠勤若此，見思安之悖慢何如！」
units.en: Compare Mingyuan's loyalty and diligence with this, and see how Si'an's insolence and neglect measure up!"
units.literal: When one compares Mingyuan's loyalty and diligence like this, how does it compare to Si'an's defiance and negligence!"

units.zh: 其見賞如此。
units.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
units.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

units.zh: 其後，遷鄭州刺史，監大軍於河上。
units.en: Thereafter he was transferred to Zheng Prefecture to supervise the army on the Yellow River front.
units.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to Zheng Prefecture to oversee the army on the river.

units.zh: 梁末帝以戴思遠為北面招討使。
units.en: The last Liang emperor appointed Dai Siyuan commander-in-chief of the northern campaign.
units.literal: The last Liang emperor appointed Dai Siyuan northern campaign commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 行師不利，用王彥章代之，受任之翌日，取德勝之南城，軍聲大振。
units.en: When campaigns went badly, Wang Yanzhang replaced him. The day after taking command, Yanzhang seized the southern citadel of Desheng, and army morale soared.
units.literal: Campaigns went badly, and Wang Yanzhang was put in his place. The day after assuming command he took the southern citadel of Desheng, and army morale soared.

units.zh: 張漢倫等推功於凝，凝掎摭彥章之失以間之。
units.en: Zhang Hanlun and others credited Ning with the success, and Ning seized on Yanzhang's faults to drive a wedge between them.
units.literal: Zhang Hanlun and others attributed the credit to Ning; Ning seized on Yanzhang's faults to drive a wedge between them.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：彥章棄鄒家口，復趨楊劉。
units.en: (According to the Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhang abandoned Zujiakou and hurried toward Yangliu.
units.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhang abandoned Zujiakou and hurried to Yangliu.

units.zh: 遊奕將李紹興敗梁遊兵於清邱縣南，段凝以為唐兵已自上流渡，驚駭失色，麵數彥章，尤其深入。）〉
units.en: Patrol general Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouts south of Qingqiu County. Ning concluded that Tang troops had already crossed upstream, turned pale with fright, and berated Yanzhang to his face, reproaching him above all for advancing too far.)〉
units.literal: Patrol general Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouts south of Qingqiu County. Ning thought Tang troops had already crossed upstream, turned pale with fright, and face-to-face berated Yanzhang, reproaching him especially for pushing too deep.)〉

units.zh: 梁末帝怒，罷彥章兵權。
units.en: The last Liang emperor was enraged and stripped Yanzhang of his military command.
units.literal: The last Liang emperor was angry and removed Yanzhang's military authority.

units.zh: 凝納賂於趙、張二族，求為招討使，敬翔、李振極言不可，竟不能止。
units.en: Ning bribed the Zhao and Zhang clans in pursuit of the post of campaign commander-in-chief. Jing Xiang and Li Zhen argued strenuously against the appointment but could not prevent it.
units.literal: Ning bribed the Zhao and Zhang clans to seek the post of campaign commander-in-chief. Jing Xiang and Li Zhen strongly argued against it but could not stop it.

units.zh: 凝以眾五萬營於高陵津，裨將康延孝叛歸莊宗，延孝具陳梁軍虛實，莊宗遂決長驅之計。
units.en: Ning encamped fifty thousand men at Gaoling Ford. Subordinate general Kang Yanxiao defected to Emperor Zhuangzong and gave a full account of the Liang army's strengths and weaknesses, and Zhuangzong thereupon resolved on a direct advance.
units.literal: Ning encamped fifty thousand men at Gaoling Ford. Subordinate general Kang Yanxiao defected to Zhuangzong and fully reported the Liang army's strengths and weaknesses, whereupon Zhuangzong decided on a direct thrust.

units.zh: 未幾，莊宗入汴，凝自滑率兵而南，前鋒杜晏球至封丘，解甲聽命。
units.en: Before long Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian. Ning led troops south from Hua, and vanguard commander Du Yanqiu reached Fengqiu, laid down his arms, and awaited orders.
units.literal: Before long Zhuangzong entered Bian. Ning led troops south from Hua; vanguard commander Du Yanqiu reached Fengqiu and laid down arms awaiting orders.

units.zh: 翌日，凝率大軍乞降於汴郊，莊宗釋之，復以凝為滑州兵馬留後，賜姓，名紹欽。
units.en: The next day Ning led the main army to surrender in the suburbs of Bian. Emperor Zhuangzong spared him, reappointed him military reserve officer of Hua Prefecture, granted him the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaoqin.
units.literal: The next day Ning led the main army to surrender in the Bian suburbs. Zhuangzong spared him, restored him as military reserve officer of Hua Prefecture, granted the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaoqin.

units.zh: 有頃，正授節度，改兗州節度使。
units.en: Shortly thereafter he received a full appointment as military commissioner and was transferred to Yanzhou.
units.literal: Shortly thereafter he received full commission as military commissioner and was transferred to Yanzhou.

units.zh: 凝初見莊宗，因伶人景進通貨於宮掖。
units.en: When Ning first met Emperor Zhuangzong, he used the actor Jing Jin to convey gifts into the inner palace.
units.literal: When Ning first met Zhuangzong, through the actor Jing Jin he conveyed goods into the inner palace.

units.zh: 凝天性奸佞，巧言飾智，善候人意。
units.en: By nature Ning was treacherous and sycophantic, skilled at polished speech and feigned wisdom, and adept at reading what others wished to hear.
units.literal: By nature Ning was treacherous and sycophantic, skilled at artful speech and feigned wisdom, adept at reading others' wishes.

units.zh: 其年，契丹寇幽州，命宣徽使李紹宏監護諸軍，以禦契丹，凝與董璋戍瓦橋關。
units.en: That year the Khitan raided Youzhou. Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed to oversee the armies against them; Ning and Dong Zhang garrisoned Waqiao Pass.
units.literal: That year the Khitan raided Youzhou. Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed to oversee all armies against the Khitan; Ning and Dong Zhang garrisoned Waqiao Pass.

units.zh: 凝巧事紹宏，紹宏嘗乘間奏凝蓋世奇才，可以大任，屢請以兵柄委之。
units.en: Ning skillfully ingratiated himself with Shaohong, who on one occasion memorialized that Ning was a rare genius fit for great responsibility and repeatedly asked that military command be entrusted to him.
units.literal: Ning skillfully ingratiated himself with Shaohong, who once found occasion to memorialize that Ning was a rare genius fit for great responsibility and repeatedly asked that military authority be entrusted to him.

units.zh: 郭崇韜曰：「段凝亡國敗軍之將，奸諂難狀，不要信也。」
units.en: Guo Chongtao said, "Duan Ning is a defeated general of a ruined state; his treachery and flattery are beyond description—do not trust him."
units.literal: Guo Chongtao said: "Duan Ning is a defeated general of a ruined state; his treachery and flattery are beyond description—do not trust him."

units.zh: 凝在藩鎮，私用庫物數萬計，有司促償，中旨貰其負。
units.en: At his fief Ning privately used treasury goods worth tens of thousands. When the relevant office pressed for repayment, an imperial order remitted his debt.
units.literal: At his fief Ning privately used treasury goods numbering in the tens of thousands. The relevant office pressed for repayment, but an imperial order remitted his debt.

units.zh: 同光三年四月，移授鄧州節度使。
units.en: In the fourth month of the third year of Tongguang he was transferred to military commissioner of Deng Prefecture.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Tongguang he was transferred to military commissioner of Deng Prefecture.

units.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮據鄴城，李紹宏請用凝為大將，莊宗許之，令具方略條奏。
units.en: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili seized Ye City. Li Shaohong asked that Ning be appointed commander; Emperor Zhuangzong agreed and ordered him to submit a detailed plan.
units.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili held Ye City. Li Shaohong asked to use Ning as commander; Zhuangzong agreed and ordered him to submit a detailed plan.

units.zh: 凝所請偏裨皆取其己黨，莊宗疑之，乃止。
units.en: Every subordinate commander Ning requested was from his own faction. Emperor Zhuangzong grew suspicious and halted the appointment.
units.literal: All the subordinate commanders Ning requested were his own faction. Zhuangzong grew suspicious and stopped the appointment.

units.zh: 明宗至洛陽，霍彥威怒其前事，與溫韜同收下獄，詔釋之，放歸田里。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong reached Luoyang, Huo Yanwei, angry at his past conduct, had him imprisoned together with Wen Tao. An edict released them and sent them back to their homes.
units.literal: When Mingzong reached Luoyang, Huo Yanwei, angry at his past conduct, had him imprisoned together with Wen Tao. An edict released them and sent them home.

units.zh: 明年，竄於遼州，竟與溫韜同製賜死。
units.en: The following year he fled to Liaozhou and was ultimately, by edict together with Wen Tao, commanded to take his own life.
units.literal: The next year he fled to Liaozhou and in the end was by edict together with Wen Tao ordered to take his own life.

units.zh: 孔謙，
units.en: Kong Qian,
units.literal: Kong Qian,

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》作魏州人。）〉
units.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian gives his nativity as Weizhou.)〉
units.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian gives his nativity as Weizhou.)〉

units.zh: 莊宗同光初，為租庸副使。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era under Emperor Zhuangzong, he served as deputy commissioner of taxation and corvée.
units.literal: Early in the Tongguang era under Zhuangzong, he served as deputy commissioner of taxation and corvée.

units.zh: 謙本州之幹吏，上自天祐十二年，帝平定魏博，會計皆委製置。
units.en: Qian had been a capable clerk in the prefecture. From the twelfth year of Tianyou, when the emperor pacified Weibo, all fiscal accounting was placed under his management.
units.literal: Qian was originally a capable clerk of the prefecture. From the twelfth year of Tianyou, when the emperor pacified Weibo, all accounting was entrusted to his management.

units.zh: 謙能曲事權要，效其才力，帝委以泉貨之務，設法箕斂，七八年間，軍儲獲濟。
units.en: Qian knew how to defer skillfully to the powerful and put his talents to use. The emperor entrusted him with fiscal affairs; he devised methods of heavy exaction, and over seven or eight years the army's stores were kept supplied.
units.literal: Qian could defer skillfully to the powerful and apply his talents. The emperor entrusted him with fiscal affairs; he devised methods of heavy exaction, and over seven or eight years army stores were supplied.

units.zh: 及帝即位於鄴城，謙已當為租庸使。
units.en: When the emperor took the throne at Ye City, Qian ought already to have become commissioner of taxation and corvée.
units.literal: When the emperor acceded at Ye City, Qian ought already to have become commissioner of taxation and corvée.

units.zh: 物議以謙雖有經營濟贍之勞，然人地尚卑，不欲驟總重任。
units.en: Public opinion held that although Qian had worked hard to manage and supply provisions, his rank and standing were still too low, and people did not want to see him suddenly given chief responsibility.
units.literal: Public opinion held that although Qian had labored to manage and supply provisions, his person and position were still low, and people did not wish to see him suddenly given chief responsibility.

units.zh: 樞密使郭崇韜舉魏博觀察判官張憲為租庸使，以謙為副，謙悒然不樂者久之。
units.en: Guo Chongtao, director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, recommended Zhang Xian, observation commissioner aide of Weibo, as commissioner of taxation and corvée and made Qian his deputy. Qian remained displeased for a long time.
units.literal: Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Guo Chongtao recommended Zhang Xian, observation commissioner aide of Weibo, as commissioner of taxation and corvée and made Qian deputy. Qian was displeased for a long time.

units.zh: 帝既平梁汴，謙徑自魏州馳之行在，因謂崇韜曰：「魏都重地，須大臣彈壓，以謙籌之，非張憲不可。」
units.en: After the emperor had pacified Liang and Bian, Qian raced directly from Weizhou to the imperial camp and told Chongtao, "Ye is a critical territory and requires a senior minister to keep order. As I see it, no one but Zhang Xian will do."
units.literal: After the emperor had pacified Liang and Bian, Qian raced directly from Weizhou to the imperial camp and said to Chongtao: "Ye is a critical territory and requires a senior minister to keep order. Considering the matter, none but Zhang Xian will do."

units.zh: 崇韜以為忠告，即奏憲為鄴都副留守，乃命宰臣豆盧革專判租庸。
units.en: Chongtao took this as sincere counsel, immediately memorialized Zhang Xian as deputy garrison commander of Ye, and ordered chief minister Dou Lüge to oversee taxation and corvée exclusively.
units.literal: Chongtao took this as sincere counsel, immediately memorialized Zhang Xian as deputy garrison commander of Ye, and ordered chief minister Dou Lüge to oversee taxation and corvée exclusively.

units.zh: 謙彌失望，乃尋革過失。
units.en: Qian was all the more disappointed and set about looking for Ge's faults.
units.literal: Qian was all the more disappointed and therefore sought out Ge's faults.

units.zh: 時革以手書便省庫錢數十萬，謙以手書示崇韜，亦辭避。
units.en: At the time Ge had used a personal note to draw several hundred thousand from the treasury for convenience. Qian showed the note to Chongtao, who also declined the post.
units.literal: At the time Ge had used a personal note to draw several hundred thousand from the treasury for convenience. Qian showed the note to Chongtao, who also declined the post.

units.zh: 帝問：「當委何人為可？」
units.en: The emperor asked, "To whom should I entrust this office?"
units.literal: The emperor asked: "To whom should I entrust this office?"

units.zh: 崇韜曰：「孔謙雖久掌貨泉，然物議未當居大任，以臣所見，當委張憲為便。」
units.en: Chongtao said, "Although Kong Qian has long managed fiscal affairs, public opinion holds that he should not yet hold great responsibility. In my view Zhang Xian would be the better choice."
units.literal: Chongtao said: "Although Kong Qian has long managed fiscal affairs, public opinion holds that he should not yet hold great responsibility. In my view Zhang Xian would be appropriate."

units.zh: 帝促征之。
units.en: The emperor urgently summoned him.
units.literal: The emperor urgently summoned him.

units.zh: 憲性精辨，為趨時者所忌，人不祐之。
units.en: Zhang was by nature sharp and discerning; those who curried favor resented him, and no one came to his support.
units.literal: Zhang was by nature sharp and discerning; those who curried favor resented him, and no one supported him.

units.zh: 謙乘間訴於豆盧革曰：「租庸錢穀，悉在眼前，委一小吏可辦。
units.en: Qian seized an opportunity to complain to Dou Lüge: "The revenues and grain of taxation and corvée are all right before one's eyes; a minor clerk could handle the task.
units.literal: Qian seized an opportunity to complain to Dou Lüge: "The revenues and grain of taxation and corvée are all right before one's eyes; entrusting a minor clerk would suffice.

units.zh: 鄴都本根之地，不可輕付於人。
units.en: Ye is the foundation of the realm and must not be lightly entrusted to anyone.
units.literal: Ye is the foundation of the realm and must not be lightly entrusted to anyone.

units.zh: 興唐尹王正言無裨益之才，徒有獨行，詔書既征張憲，復以何人為代？」
units.en: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan lacks talent of real use and possesses only a reputation for integrity. Now that an edict has summoned Zhang Xian, who is to replace him?"
units.literal: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan lacks talent of real use and possesses only a reputation for integrity. Now that an edict has summoned Zhang Xian, who shall replace him?"

units.zh: 豆盧革言於崇韜，崇韜曰：「鄴都分司列職，皆主上舊人，委王正言何慮不辦？」
units.en: Dou Lüge spoke to Chongtao, who said, "All the branch offices and posts at Ye are the emperor's old associates; if Wang Zhengyan is entrusted with the task, why worry that he cannot manage it?"
units.literal: Dou Lüge spoke to Chongtao, who said: "All the branch offices and posts at Ye are the emperor's old associates; entrusting Wang Zhengyan—why worry that he cannot manage it?"

units.zh: 革曰：「俱是失也，設不獲已，以正言掌租庸，取書於大臣，或可辦矣；
units.en: Ge said, "Both choices would be mistakes. If there is no help for it, let Zhengyan manage taxation and corvée while taking counsel from senior ministers—that might work;
units.literal: Ge said: "Both choices would be mistakes. If there is no help for it, let Zhengyan manage taxation and corvée while taking counsel from senior ministers—that might work;

units.zh: 若付之方面，必敗人事。」
units.en: but if entrusted with a regional command, he is sure to ruin affairs."
units.literal: if entrusted with a regional command, he is sure to ruin affairs."

units.zh: 謙以正言非德非勳，懦而易製，曰：「此議為便。」
units.en: Qian, knowing Zhengyan lacked virtue and merit and was cowardly and easy to control, said, "This plan is convenient."
units.literal: Qian, knowing Zhengyan lacked virtue and merit and was cowardly and easy to control, said: "This plan is convenient."

units.zh: 然非己誌。
units.en: Yet it was not what he wanted.
units.literal: Yet it was not his wish.

units.zh: 尋掎正言之失，泣訴於崇韜，厚賂閹伶，以求進用，人知奸諂，沮之，乃上章請退。
units.en: Before long he seized on Zhengyan's faults and tearfully complained to Chongtao, bribed eunuch actors heavily to seek advancement; when people recognized his treachery and flattery they blocked him, and he submitted a memorial asking to retire.
units.literal: Before long he seized on Zhengyan's faults and tearfully complained to Chongtao, bribed eunuch actors heavily to seek advancement; when people recognized his treachery and flattery they blocked him, and he submitted a memorial asking to retire.

units.zh: 帝怒其規避，將置於法，樂人景進於帝前解喻而止。
units.en: The emperor was angry at his evasion and was about to punish him by law, but the musician Jing Jin explained matters before the emperor and stopped it.
units.literal: The emperor was angry at his evasion and was about to punish him by law, but the musician Jing Jin explained matters before the emperor and stopped it.

units.zh: 王正言風病恍惚，不能綜三司事，景進屢言於帝，乃以正言守禮部尚書，以謙為租庸使。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan suffered from wind ailment and mental confusion and could not manage the three offices. Jing Jin repeatedly spoke to the emperor, whereupon Zhengyan was made Minister of Rites and Qian was made commissioner of taxation and corvée.
units.literal: Wang Zhengyan suffered from wind ailment and mental confusion and could not manage the three offices. Jing Jin repeatedly spoke to the emperor, whereupon Zhengyan was made Minister of Rites and Qian was made commissioner of taxation and corvée.

units.zh: 謙以國用不足，奏：「諸道判官員數過多，請隻置節度、觀察、判官、書記、支使、推官各一員。
units.en: Citing insufficient state revenue, Qian memorialized: "The number of aides in the various circuits is excessive. I request that each circuit be limited to one military commissioner aide, one observation commissioner aide, one secretary, one staff officer, and one investigative officer.
units.literal: Qian, citing insufficient state revenue, memorialized: "The number of aides in the various circuits is excessive. Request to appoint only one each of military commissioner aide, observation commissioner aide, secretary, staff officer, and investigative officer per circuit.

units.zh: 留守置判官各一員。
units.en: Garrison commanders were to have one aide each.
units.literal: Garrison commanders to have one aide each.

units.zh: 三京府置判官、推官，餘並罷俸錢。」
units.en: The three capital prefectures were to have aides and investigative officers; salaries for all other such posts were to be abolished."
units.literal: The three capital prefectures to have aides and investigative officers; all others to have salaries abolished."

units.zh: 又奏：「百官俸錢雖多，折支非實，請減半數，皆支實錢。」
units.en: He also memorialized: "Although official salaries are nominally large, payment in kind does not reflect real value. I request that salaries be cut by half and paid entirely in cash."
units.literal: He also memorialized: "Although official salaries are large, disbursement in kind is not real value. Request to cut salaries by half and pay all in cash."

units.zh: 並從之。
units.en: All were approved.
units.literal: All were approved.

units.zh: 未幾，半年俸復從虛折。
units.en: Before long, half-year salaries were again paid in kind at inflated rates.
units.literal: Before long, half-year salaries were again paid in kind at inflated rates.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下原闕。
units.en: (Note: the original text below is missing.
units.literal: (Note: the original text below is missing.

units.zh: 《北夢瑣言》：明宗即位，誅租庸使孔謙等。
units.en: Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he executed commissioner of taxation and corvée Kong Qian and others.
units.literal: Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams: When Mingzong took the throne, he executed commissioner of taxation and corvée Kong Qian and others.

units.zh: 孔謙者，魏州孔目。
units.en: Kong Qian had been a clerical officer in Weizhou.
units.literal: Kong Qian was a clerical officer of Weizhou.

units.zh: 莊宗圖霸，以供饋兵食，謙有力焉。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pursued hegemony, Qian contributed greatly to supplying the army with provisions.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pursued hegemony, Qian contributed greatly to supplying army provisions.

units.zh: 既為租庸使，曲事嬖幸，奪宰相權，專以聚斂為意，剝削為端。
units.en: Once he became commissioner, he deferentially served the emperor's favorites, usurped the chancellor's authority, and devoted himself to accumulation and exploitation.
units.literal: Once commissioner, he deferentially served favorites, usurped the chancellor's authority, and devoted himself to accumulation and exploitation.

units.zh: 以犯眾怒，伏誅。）〉
units.en: Provoking universal anger, he was executed.)〉
units.literal: Provoking universal anger, he was executed.)〉

units.zh: 李鄴，魏州人也。
units.en: Li Ye came from Weizhou.
units.literal: Li Ye was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 幼事楊師厚，及莊宗入魏，漸轉裨將，曆數郡刺史，後遷亳州。
units.en: In youth he served Yang Shihou. When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei he gradually rose to subordinate general, served in turn as prefect of several commanderies, and was later transferred to Bozhou.
units.literal: In youth he served Yang Shihou; when Zhuangzong entered Wei he gradually rose to subordinate general, served successively as prefect of several commanderies, and was later transferred to Bozhou.

units.zh: 為政貪穢，有奴為人持金以賂鄴，奴隱其金，鄴殺之。
units.en: His governance was greedy and corrupt. A slave held gold on someone's behalf to bribe Ye; the slave kept the gold for himself, and Ye killed him.
units.literal: His governance was greedy and corrupt. A slave held gold on someone's behalf to bribe Ye; the slave kept the gold for himself, and Ye killed him.

units.zh: 其家上訴，因訐其陰事，詔貶郴州司戶參軍，又貶崖州長流百姓，所在賜自盡。
units.en: The family appealed upward; on account of denunciations of his secret misdeeds, an edict demoted him to registrar of Chen Prefecture. He was further demoted and exiled to Yazhou as a commoner, and wherever he went was ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: The family appealed upward; on account of denunciations of his secret misdeeds, an edict demoted him to registrar of Chen Prefecture; he was further demoted and exiled to Yazhou as a commoner, and wherever he went was ordered to take his own life.

units.zh: 史臣曰：《易》云：「積不善之家，必有餘殃。」
units.en: The historian says: The Book of Changes states, "A house that accumulates nothing good is sure to have surplus calamity."
units.literal: The historian says: The Book of Changes states: "A house that accumulates nothing good is sure to have surplus calamity."

units.zh: 又曰：「惡不積不足以滅身。」
units.en: It also says, "Evil not accumulated is insufficient to destroy one's person."
units.literal: It also says: "Evil not accumulated is insufficient to destroy one's person."

units.zh: 如毛璋之儔，可謂積惡而滅其身矣，況溫韜之發陵寢，段凝之敗國家，罪不容誅，死猶差晚。
units.en: Men like Mao Zhang may be said to have accumulated evil until it destroyed them; how much more Wen Tao, who opened imperial tombs, and Duan Ning, who ruined the state—their crimes were beyond what execution could answer, and even death came too late.
units.literal: Men like Mao Zhang may be said to have accumulated evil and destroyed themselves; how much more Wen Tao, who opened imperial tombs, and Duan Ning, who ruined the state—their crimes could not be forgiven by execution, and even death came too late.

units.zh: 餘皆瑣瑣，何足議焉。
units.en: The rest are trifling matters, unworthy of discussion.
units.literal: The rest are trifling matters, unworthy of discussion.

units.zh: 己卯，以宣義軍節度副大使、知節度事、北面行營副招討等使、特進、檢校太傅霍彥威為天平軍節度副大使，知節度事。
units.en: On jimao, Huo Yanwei—deputy commissioner of Xuanyi, acting military commissioner, deputy northern pacification commissioner, specially advanced, and honorary Grand Mentor—was named deputy commissioner of Tianping with charge of military affairs.
units.literal: On jimao, Xuanyi Army deputy commissioner, acting military commissioner, Northern Line deputy pacification commissioner, specially advanced, honorary Grand Mentor Huo Yanwei was made Tianping Army deputy commissioner, acting military commissioner.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 初，學士竇夢征草錢鏐麻，貶蓬萊尉，帝召專入翰林，遣崇政使李振問宰相云：「專是宰臣蕭頃女婿，令中書商量可否？」
units.en: Earlier, Dou Mengzheng had drafted Qian Liu's edict and was banished to Penglai; the Emperor now summoned Zhuan to the Hanlin and sent Li Zhen to ask: "Zhuan is Xiao Qing's son-in-law—should the Secretariat weigh this?"
units.literal: Earlier, academician Dou Mengzheng had drafted Qian Liu's appointment edict and was demoted to subprefect of Penglai; the Emperor summoned Zhuan into the Hanlin and sent Chongzheng commissioner Li Zhen to ask the chancellors: "Zhuan is Chancellor Xiao Qing's son-in-law—should the Secretariat discuss whether this is permissible?"

units.zh: 夏四月丁未，以宣徽院使、右衛上將軍趙縠權知青州軍州事，以宣徽院副使韋堅權知本院事。
units.en: On dingwei in the fourth month of summer, Zhao Gu, Xuanhui Court commissioner and Right Guard senior general, was made acting commissioner for Qingzhou's military and prefectural affairs; Xuanhui Court deputy commissioner Wei Jian was made acting head of that court.
units.literal: On dingwei in the fourth month of summer, Xuanhui Court commissioner and Right Guard senior general Zhao Gu was made acting Qing prefect military and prefectural commissioner; Xuanhui Court deputy commissioner Wei Jian was made acting head of that court.

units.zh: 甲寅，以刑部郎中、充史館修撰竇專為翰林學士。
units.en: On jiayin, Dou Zhuan, Ministry of Punishments director and History Office compiler, entered the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: On jiayin, Ministry of Punishments bureau director and History Office compiler Dou Zhuan was made Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 乙卯，以樞密使趙敬怡權知汴州軍州事。
units.en: On yimao Zhao Jingyi acted as regent at Bian.
units.literal: On yimao, Privy Commissioner Zhao Jingyi was ordered to act as regent of Bian prefecture military headquarters.

units.zh: 樞密使趙敬怡卒，贈太傅。
units.en: Zhao Jingyi died and was posthumously made grand mentor.
units.literal: Privy Commissioner Zhao Jingyi died and was posthumously given Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 以禮部尚書、興唐尹王正言依前禮部尚書，充租庸使。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan stayed Minister of Rites and was made land-tax commissioner.
units.literal: Minister of Rites and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan remained Minister of Rites and was made commissioner of land tax and corvée.

units.zh: 辛卯，以宣徽南院使、判內侍省、兼內局、特進、左監門將軍同正李紹宏為右領軍衛上將軍。
units.en: On xinmao Li Shaohong—Southern Secretariat attendant, Inner Palace overseer, Special Grandee, and Left Gate Guard general—became senior general of the Right Guard.
units.literal: On xinmao, Palace Attendant of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat, overseer of the Inner Palace, concurrent Inner Bureau, Special Grandee, and Left Gate Guard general of the same rank Li Shaohong was made senior general of the Right Imperial Guard.

units.zh: 然自此權臣愎戾，伶官用事，吏人孔謙酷加賦斂，赦文之所原放，謙復刻剝不行，大失人心，始於此矣。
units.en: Yet from then on ministers turned stubborn, actors held power, and Kong Qian re-levied what the amnesty had freed—hearts were lost from this day.
units.literal: Yet from this time powerful ministers grew obstinate, actor-officials held office, and clerk Kong Qian harshly added levies; what the amnesty had remitted Qian again exacted and would not carry out—greatly losing hearts, it began here.

units.zh: 庚午，租庸使孔謙奏：「諸道綱運客旅，多於私路苟免商稅，請令所在關防嚴加捉搦。」
units.en: On gengwu Kong Qian memorialized, "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."
units.literal: On gengwu land-tax commissioner Kong Qian memorialized: "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."

units.zh: 以鄴都副留守、興唐尹張憲檢校吏部尚書、太原尹，充北京副留守、知留守事。
units.en: Zhang Xian—Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect—became acting Personnel minister, Taiyuan prefect, and northern deputy regent in charge of regency.
units.literal: Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect Zhang Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel, Taiyuan prefect, and northern capital deputy regent with charge of regency affairs.

units.zh: 習從莊宗於河上，而镕為張文禮所弒，震從習討文禮，而家在趙，文禮執震母妻及子十餘人以招震，震不顧。
units.en: Xi followed Zhuangzong on the river while Wenli murdered Wang Rong. Zhen marched with Xi against Wenli, but his kin were still in Zhao. Wenli seized Zhen’s mother, wife, and more than ten children to force him over. Zhen would not look.
units.literal: Xi followed Zhuangzong on the river; Rong was assassinated by Zhang Wenli. Zhen followed Xi against Wenli, but his family was in Zhao. Wenli seized Zhen’s mother, wife, and more than ten children to lure Zhen; Zhen paid no attention.

units.zh: 符習，趙州昭慶人也。
units.en: Fu Xi came from Zhaqing in Zhao prefecture.
units.literal: Fu Xi was a native of Zhaqing in Zhao prefecture.

units.zh: 廷赟款稱實璋假子，有叔父在蜀，欲往省之，而無私書。
units.en: Tingyun confessed he was Zhang’s adopted son. He had an uncle in Shu and meant only to visit him. There was no secret letter.
units.literal: Tingyun confessed that he was in truth Zhang’s adopted son; he had an uncle in Shu and wished to visit him, and there was no private letter.

units.zh: 乙太府卿敬翔知崇政院，翔與帷幄之謀，故首擢焉。
units.en: Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.
units.literal: Appointing Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.

units.zh: 可改唐天祐四年為開平元年，國號大樑。
units.en: Let Tang's Tianyou year 4 become Kaiping year 1; the realm shall be called Great Liang.
units.literal: Let the fourth year of Tang's Tianyou be changed to the first year of Kaiping; the state name is Great Liang.

units.zh: 己巳，以左散騎常侍、權知開封府事邊蔚為工部侍郎，依前知府事。
units.en: On jisi Bian Wei, Left Cavalry Attendant and acting Kaifeng administrator, was made Vice Minister of Works while continuing to administer the prefecture.
units.literal: On jisi, Bian Wei, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and acting administrator of Kaifeng prefecture, was made Vice Minister of Works and continued as before to administer the prefecture.

units.zh: 己丑，以振武軍節度使、權安義留後、檢校太傅、平章事李存霸為潞州節度使，以捧日都指揮使、鄭州防禦使李紹琛為陝州節度使，以成德軍馬步軍都指揮使、右監門衛大將軍毛璋為華州節度使。
units.en: On jichou Cunba took Luzhou, Li Shaochen Shanzhou, and Mao Zhang Huazhou.
units.literal: On jichou Zhenwu military commissioner, acting Anyi regent, Grand Mentor, and chief minister Li Cunba was made Luzhou military commissioner; Sun-Rising commander and Zhengzhou defender Li Shaochen was made Shanzhou military commissioner; Chengde horse-and-foot commander and Right Gate Guard general Mao Zhang was made Huazhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 東川董璋上書言璋遣子廷赟持書往西川，疑其有奸。
units.en: Dong Zhang of Dongchuan wrote that Zhang had sent his son Tingyun west to Xichuan with a letter, and suspected treason.
units.literal: Dong Zhang of Dongchuan memorialized that Zhang had sent his son Tingyun with a letter to Xichuan, suspecting treachery.

units.zh: 明宗乃遣人追還廷赟，並璋下御史獄。
units.en: Mingzong sent men to bring Tingyun back and threw Zhang into the censor’s prison.
units.literal: Mingzong then sent men to bring Tingyun back and also cast Zhang into the censor’s prison.

units.zh: 丙寅，以西面行營馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保、鄭州刺史、充本州防禦使王彥章為檢校太傅。
units.en: On bingyin, Wang Yanzhang, Western Line horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, and Zheng prefect and defense commissioner, was promoted to honorary Grand Mentor.
units.literal: On bingyin, Western Line camp horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, Zheng prefect, and Zheng defense commissioner Wang Yanzhang was made honorary Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 是時，諸侯多不奉法，鄧州陶玘、亳州李鄴皆以贓汙論死，明宗下詔書褒廉吏普州安崇阮、洺州張萬進、耀州孫嶽等以諷天下，而以敬瑭為首。
units.en: Feudatories then flouted the law wholesale; Tao Qi of Deng and Li Ye of Bo died for graft. Mingzong published an edict holding up honest governors—An Chongruan, Zhang Wanjin, Sun Yue, and the rest—with Jingtang first among them.
units.literal: At that time many feudatories did not observe the law. Tao Qi of Dengzhou and Li Ye of Bozhou were both sentenced to death for corruption. Mingzong issued an edict praising honest officials—An Chongruan of Puzhou, Zhang Wanjin of Mingzhou, Sun Yue of Yaozhou, and others—to admonish the realm, with Jingtang at their head.

units.zh: 帝聞中都之敗，唐軍長驅將至，遣張漢倫馳驛召段凝於河上；
units.en: Hearing of Zhongdu’s fall and Tang’s advance, the Emperor dispatched Zhang Hanlun to recall Duan Ning from the river;
units.literal: The Emperor heard of Zhongdu’s defeat and that Tang troops were coming at speed; he sent Zhang Hanlun by post relay to summon Duan Ning on the river;

units.zh: 漢倫墜馬傷足，復限水潦，不能進。
units.en: Hanlun fell, injured his foot, and floods blocked him.
units.literal: Hanlun fell from his horse and injured his foot; again limited by floods, he could not advance.

units.zh: 擅收段凝、溫韜下獄，將置於法。
units.en: He took it upon himself to arrest Duan Ning and Wen Tao and throw them in prison, intending to have them executed.
units.literal: On his own authority he seized Duan Ning and Wen Tao and put them in prison, intending to punish them by law.

units.zh: 安重誨曰：「溫、段罪惡，負於梁室，眾所知矣。
units.en: An Chonghui said, "Wen and Duan are guilty men who betrayed the house of Liang, as everyone knows.
units.literal: An Chonghui said: "Wen and Duan are guilty and have wronged the house of Liang; this is known to all.

units.zh: 戊子，王彥章、杜晏球率兵急攻博州之新壘，不克，遂退保於鄒口。
units.en: On wuzi Yanzhang and Du Yanqiu failed to storm Bozhou’s new works and fell back to Zou mouth.
units.literal: On wuzi, Wang Yanzhang and Du Yanqiu led troops in urgent attack on Bozhou’s new ramparts, did not take them, then withdrew to hold Zou mouth.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.
